issues.legal_issue: A tenancy created by a mortgagee does not bind the mortgagors after redemption when the mortgage terms require return of possession and the mortgagors did not concur in a tenancy extending beyond the mortgage.
material_facts: The mortgage was anomalous and its terms required the mortgagee to return possession when the debt was repaid.

The mortgage deed permitted the mortgagee to let the property, but the permission was qualified by the obligation to return possession on redemption; the mortgagors remained liable for interest and the mortgagee was not required to let the property.
The mortgagee inducted the tenant after the mortgage was made, without the mortgagors’ concurrence in a lease that would continue after redemption.
The mortgage was redeemed while the tenant remained in possession.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy did not bind the mortgagors after redemption, and the tenant had no right to remain in possession against them.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 98 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the rights of the parties to an anomalous mortgage are determined by the mortgage deed. A tenancy granted by a mortgagee in possession may bind the mortgagors after the mortgagee’s title ends if they concurred in the grant, as recognized in Film Corporation Ltd. v. Gyan Nath. Here, the deed’s limited authorization and express requirement to return possession on redemption did not authorize a lease binding the mortgagors beyond the mortgage.

rule.if: mortgage_redemption_proceeding and mortgagee_created_tenancy and anomalous_mortgage and limited_leasing_authority and possession_return_required and not mortgagor_concurrence and not later_statutory_enlargement

predicates.mortgage_redemption_proceeding: The dispute concerns a mortgagee-created occupant’s right to remain after the mortgage is redeemed.
predicates.mortgagee_created_tenancy: A mortgagee in possession inducted the occupant as a tenant.
predicates.anomalous_mortgage: The mortgage had terms that made it an anomalous mortgage rather than a usufructuary mortgage.
predicates.limited_leasing_authority: The mortgagors authorized letting the property on terms that did not authorize a tenancy binding them after redemption.
predicates.possession_return_required: The mortgage terms required the mortgagee to return possession when the mortgage was redeemed.
predicates.mortgagor_concurrence: The mortgagors concurred in granting a tenancy that would continue after redemption.
predicates.later_statutory_enlargement: After the tenant was inducted, legislation enlarged the tenant’s rights in a way relevant to continuation after redemption.

issues.definition: If a mortgagee creates a tenancy under an anomalous mortgage, the mortgage requires return of possession on redemption, the mortgagors did not concur in a tenancy extending beyond redemption, and no later legislation enlarged the tenant’s rights, the tenant has no continuing right against the mortgagors.

issues.legal_issue: Rent-control legislation already in force when a mortgagee inducted a tenant does not constitute a later statutory enlargement of that tenant’s rights.
material_facts: The tenant was inducted after the Saurashtra Rent Control Act had come into force.
The Bombay rent legislation later replaced the Saurashtra Act, but the relevant standard-rent and ejectment proceedings had been instituted while the Saurashtra Act remained in force.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s rights were not enlarged by legislation enacted after the tenancy was granted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court recognized the principle, reflected in Mahabir Gope v. Harbans Narain, Asa Ram v. Ram Kali, Dahya Lal v. Rasul Mohammed Abdul Rahim, and Prabhu v. Ram Dev, and summarized in Mulla’s Transfer of Property Act, that a later statutory enlargement of a tenant’s rights may affect whether a mortgagee-created tenancy binds the mortgagor beyond the mortgage. That principle did not apply because the relevant rent-control protection was already in force when the tenant was inducted; the later replacement of that legislation did not enlarge the tenant’s rights for these proceedings.

rule.if: mortgagee_tenancy_dispute and tenant_inducted_by_mortgagee and rent_protection_already_in_force and not later_statutory_enlargement

predicates.mortgagee_tenancy_dispute: The dispute concerns the effect of rent-control protection on a tenancy created by a mortgagee in possession.
predicates.tenant_inducted_by_mortgagee: A mortgagee in possession placed the tenant in the property.
predicates.rent_protection_already_in_force: Rent-control protection applied when the tenant was inducted.
predicates.later_statutory_enlargement: Legislation enacted after the tenant was inducted enlarged the tenant’s rights relevant to the dispute.

issues.definition: Where a mortgagee-created tenant received rent-control protection from the outset and no later legislation enlarged the tenant’s rights, the tenant’s rights were not enlarged after induction.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant whose possession derives solely from a mortgagee and who has no independent rights need not be joined to post-redemption execution proceedings against the mortgagee.
material_facts: The mortgage was redeemed and the mortgagors sought possession through execution proceedings against the mortgagee.
The tenant had been inducted by the mortgagee and was not made a party to the suit or execution application.
The tenant had no independent right to possession against the mortgagors.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was not a necessary party, and the execution proceedings against the mortgagee were binding on the tenant.
issues.legal_principle: An occupant whose rights derive from a mortgagee and are co-terminous with the mortgagee’s rights has no independent right that requires the occupant to be joined; the occupant’s position is akin to that of a subtenant whose rights end with those of the tenant. The Court applied this principle to the execution proceedings following redemption.

rule.if: execution_after_mortgage_redemption and occupant_inducted_by_mortgagee and not occupant_has_independent_possession_right

predicates.execution_after_mortgage_redemption: Execution proceedings were brought to obtain possession after the mortgage was redeemed.
predicates.occupant_inducted_by_mortgagee: The occupant’s possession began under a tenancy created by the mortgagee.
predicates.occupant_has_independent_possession_righ: The occupant held a right to possession independent of the mortgagee’s rights.

issues.definition: If an occupant was inducted by the mortgagee, has no independent right to possession, and execution seeks possession after redemption, the occupant need not be joined and the execution binds the occupant.

issues.legal_issue: Permission given to a mortgagee to let mortgaged property does not, by itself, make the mortgagee the mortgagors’ agent.
material_facts: The mortgagors and mortgagee stood in a debtor-creditor relationship under the mortgage.
The mortgage deed permitted the mortgagee to let the property, subject to the mortgage terms.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagee was not the mortgagors’ agent, and the mortgagors were not bound as principals by the tenancy on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the relationship between mortgagor and mortgagee remained one of debtor and creditor; the authority to lease the property did not constitute an agency relationship.

predicates.mortgage_relationship: The parties’ relationship arose from a mortgage of property.
predicates.debtor_creditor_relationship: The mortgage created a relationship of debtor and creditor between the parties.
predicates.leasing_permission: The mortgagors permitted the mortgagee to let the mortgaged property.

issues.definition: When a mortgage creates a debtor-creditor relationship and includes permission to let the property, that permission does not make the mortgagee the mortgagors’ agent.
